narrative_purpose: Shows what propulsive efficiency looks like from behind: a narrow chain of small fast vortex rings against a broad train of wide gentle vortex loops.
subject: Two horizontal bands of dark water, one above the other, each showing a wake trailing away to the left behind a partly visible propulsor at the right edge. In the upper band, a small smooth biological nozzle has left a narrow straight chain of eight tightly spaced small doughnut-shaped vortex rings, each ring compact and sharply defined, glowing brightly, with the water immediately around the chain badly churned into fine turbulent froth. In the lower band, a broad curved muscular wing tip has left a wide train of four very large soft oval vortex loops, widely spaced, faint and diffuse, the surrounding water smooth and almost undisturbed.
scene: Deep dark open water with no surface or floor visible, the two wakes isolated for comparison.
camera: Flat straight-on lateral view, both bands seen edge-on at the same scale.
light: The vortex structures themselves are the light source, revealed by fine suspended bioluminescent particles caught in the rotation; ambient water almost black.
palette: Void indigo water, bright Pandora cyan in the tight fast rings, dim soft teal in the broad gentle loops, faint mist grey in the turbulent froth.
style: Painterly flow-visualisation plate, as if a naturalist had photographed glowing plankton caught in two wakes.
detail_level: Crisp on the ring geometry and spacing in both bands; the propulsors at the right edge only partly shown and less detailed.
composition: Two stacked horizontal registers of equal height, wakes running right to left in both, plain black water at the left end of each band framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: The two wakes must differ clearly in ring size, spacing and brightness: upper small tight bright and many, lower large sparse faint and few. Same palette in both bands.
